narrative:
Your loan application was denied because the model estimated a 51% chance that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning it was slightly more confident you would struggle to repay than not. This decision was primarily driven by your checking account status, which shows a negative balance (under 0 Deutsche Marks). Among approved applicants, only about 20% had a negative balance, while half had no checking account at all, making this the single most influential factor in the model’s decision.

To understand what would change this outcome, we explored "what if" scenarios—small, realistic adjustments that would flip the prediction to "good credit." Only one such scenario was found, and it required changing just one feature: your checking account status. If your account had no balance (neither positive nor negative), the model would approve your loan. This means the negative balance is the critical red flag, outweighing other factors like your credit history (which is actually strong—you have no credits and all paid off) or your low requested amount of 1,108 DM (far below the average of 2,887 DM for approved applicants).

Other features, such as your 12-month loan duration, employment of 4-7 years, or owning real estate, did not need to change in any scenario. This shows the model focuses heavily on your immediate financial liquidity rather than your long-term stability. Your savings under 100 DM and installment rate of 4% (higher than the average 2.94% for approved applicants) were also not flagged as issues, likely because your low loan amount and good credit history offset them.

To get approved, the most actionable step is to improve your checking account balance. Even moving from a negative balance to zero—without needing savings or a higher income—would be enough. This is a realistic change you can make by depositing funds to clear the negative status. Once your account shows no deficit, the model would see you as a low-risk borrower, similar to the 50% of approved applicants who also had no checking account balance. Focus on this single adjustment, and your application would likely be accepted.
